conviction_note: Every external read on the May-July quarter improved after SWBI last spoke on 2026-06-17 (fiscal-Q1 adjusted NICS +7.7% y/y vs +1.2% in the quarter just reported at +26.7% revenue; Ruger sell-through +19%; Sportsman's Warehouse firearms +8.7%), consensus is only +16% revenue, and yet the stock has de-rated 16% in 20 sessions with no company release and no August SEC filing while the 25-delta skew is -0.67 - so I take about a third of the implied 13.16% move to the upside and haircut for the fact that I could not source the de-rate.

findings.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SWBI's exact fiscal Q1 (May+June+July 2026) totalled 3,290,647 against 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.70% y/y - a 6.5-point acceleration from the +1.20% in the Feb-Apr quarter on which SWBI just printed revenue +26.7% and handgun sell-in +23.2%, while consensus looks for only +16% revenue growth off an $85.1M base.
findings.why_not_priced: The July single-month headline (+8.5%) was NSSF-press-released and is in the wire, but the three-month fiscal-quarter aggregate and the bridge from it to SWBI's own realised sell-in ratio is published nowhere. The validation is that the company's Q4 release cited 'NICS increased only 1.1%' for Feb-Apr and my computed figure for that window is +1.20% - so this identical series, one quarter later, is the number management will read out tonight, and it is six points better. If the street had run this arithmetic the sell-side revenue bar would not sit 11 points BELOW the growth the company delivered last quarter on a demand backdrop six points weaker, and the stock would not be -16.35% over 20 sessions with 25-delta call skew (-0.67) into the print.
findings.independence: Sturm Ruger's 2026-07-29 release, filed after SWBI last spoke, reports estimated distributor-to-retailer sell-through of its own products +19% in Apr-Jun (two of SWBI's three months) against adjusted NICS +5%: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results . Ruger's cited NICS comparator derives from the same NSSF series as this finding; the sell-through and unit-inventory figures do not.

findings.finding: Both channel layers turned positive in SWBI's exact quarter, and both datapoints were published after SWBI last spoke: Ruger's distributor inventories fell 45,800 units and finished goods 100,100 units on sell-through +19% (2026-07-29), and Sportsman's Warehouse's 10-Q for the 13 weeks ended 2026-08-01 shows firearm sales +$5.2M / +8.7% and ammunition +$3.9M / +9.9% (filed 2026-09-01).
findings.why_not_priced: SWBI's last guidance-bearing statement was 2026-06-17, when it framed FY2027 industry demand as 'slightly higher' than FY2026. Both of these prints post-date that and both are better than 'slightly higher', and channel de-stock has been the bear case on SWBI for six quarters - the paragraph that would move the stock is the channel-inventory paragraph, not EPS. Visible evidence it is not priced: SWBI fell 7.97% in the five sessions that contain SPWH's 2026-09-01 print, on which SPWH shares rose - a same-category retailer's firearms acceleration was published and SWBI's equity went the other way.
findings.independence: Independent of the NICS series and of finding 1's mechanism - these are physical unit inventories at a distributor and dollar comps at a retailer, from two different filers. Ruger source: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results . Caveat that cuts the other way: SPWH reaffirmed rather than raised FY guidance (-1.0% to +2.0% comps, $30-36M EBITDA) in its 2026-09-01 release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/01/3354585/30783/en/sportsman-s-warehouse-holdings-inc-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results.html

findings.finding: On 2026-08-05 the N.D. Texas entered final judgment and a permanent injunction in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF holding NFA registration of suppressors/SBRs/SBSs unconstitutional after the tax went to zero; the stay expired 2026-08-12 and DOJ declined an emergency appeal - three weeks after SWBI's 2026-07-15 investor day told investors suppressors were its fastest-growing lane at +95.6% revenue growth in H1 CY2026 into a $700M-$950M TAM, with July NFA-category NICS checks +108.8% y/y to 130,013.
findings.why_not_priced: The entire coverage set for this ruling is gun-law media, NRA-ILA and law-firm client alerts; not one financial-press item in my searches connects it to SWBI, and the SWBI preview copy in the wire is pure consensus revenue/EPS. It is also a forward item - it post-dates the printed quarter - so it can only enter the price through tonight's call, where management will be asked about the one growth lane it spent its investor day on. If the market had connected the two, a stock whose newest disclosed growth engine just had its principal regulatory friction enjoined would not carry -0.67 skew and a 16% 20-day de-rate.
findings.independence: NSSF's own 2026-08-17 FFL guidance confirms the ruling is live but that the industry is in compliance limbo, which is why I band this two-sided rather than purely positive: https://www.nssf.org/articles/nssf-guidance-on-nfa-transfers/ . Overlap disclosure: the +108.8% NFA-check figure comes from the same NSSF monthly release family as finding 1, so treat the NFA-check number as part of that source cluster; the court ruling and the investor-day suppressor growth rate (SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092796/000119312526304020/d30687dex991.htm) are separate documents.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the 16.35% 20-day / 7.97% 5-day de-rate: no company press release since the 2026-08-20 scheduling alert, and EDGAR shows literally no SWBI filing in August 2026 other than the DEF 14A/DEFA14A/ARS on 2026-08-06 - no 8-K, no S-3, no 424B, no Form 4. I could not source the decline and that unexplained gap is the main cap on my conviction

August 2026 NICS/NSSF-adjusted figure - not published as of 2026-09-03; a search hit reporting 'August, 1,091,342, down 9.9%' is The Reload on August 2025 data (the CSV confirms 2025-08 = 1,091,342), a year-relabelling trap I discarded
Insider activity - no Form 4 since 2026-06-17, so no insider buying on the way down and no cluster either way

A read-through from American Outdoor Brands, the spun-off sibling with an identical May-July quarter - it reports the same day at the same hour (2026-09-03 amc, 5:00pm ET call), so nothing is available in advance
SWBI consumer rebate/promotion page (404 at /promotions) - could not establish whether discounting intensified in the quarter
FBI month/year-by-type NICS PDF for a handgun-only quarterly cut - 403 from fbi.gov; SWBI's mix is handgun-heavy so a handgun-specific rate would have sharpened finding 1
Any 2026 restructuring, layoff or Springfield-consolidation event that would produce an unguided Q1 charge - nothing after the 2021-2023 Maryville move
Any product recall or safety notice dated 2026 - the live recall pages are all older (M&P12, Shield EZ, Model 22A, I-Bolt)
baseline_tension: It cuts squarely against the run-up and mildly with the skew: the tape has SWBI down 16% in 20 sessions on no sourceable news while every external read on the quarter improved, and the -0.67 skew says the option market is paying more for upside than downside, so the derivatives and my findings agree while the equity tape disagrees with both.
